+"""Weight parsing for shipping.
+
+Warehouse staff type package weights in by hand ("2.5 kg", "12 oz"); parse_weight
+normalises them to whole grams so carrier integrations always see the same unit.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
+
+# Grams per unit, as exact decimals (oz is the official avoirdupois ounce; lb is
+# 16 x oz so it converts with the same factor as the spec gives).
+_GRAMS_PER_UNIT = {
+    "g": Decimal(1),
+    "kg": Decimal(1000),
+    "lb": Decimal("453.59237"),
+    "oz": Decimal("28.349523125"),
+}
+
+_WEIGHT_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)\s*([a-zA-Z]+)\s*$")
+
+
+def parse_weight(text: str) -> int:
+    """Parse a staff-entered weight ("2.5 kg") and return it in whole grams.
+
+    Accepts an integer or "."-separated decimal, optional whitespace, then a
+    unit: g, kg, lb or oz (case-insensitive). Leading/trailing whitespace is
+    ignored. The result is rounded to the nearest gram (0.5 rounds up).
+
+    Raises ValueError for a missing number, missing/unknown unit, a negative
+    value or "," as decimal separator.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(text, str):
+        raise ValueError(f"weight must be a string, not {type(text).__name__}")
+
+    match = _WEIGHT_RE.match(text)
+    if match is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"unrecognised weight {text!r}")
+
+    number, unit = match.group(1), match.group(2).lower()
+    factor = _GRAMS_PER_UNIT.get(unit)
+    if factor is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"unknown weight unit {unit!r} in {text!r}")
+
+    grams = Decimal(number) * factor
+    return int(grams.quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
